title: Reading a tree
summary: Learn the parts of a phylogenetic tree — tips, branches, nodes and the root — and what each one means, on a small tree of vertebrates.

objectives: Name the parts of a phylogenetic tree: tips, branches, nodes and the root
Read an internal node as the common ancestor of the lineages below it
Follow the direction of time from the root toward the tips

items.text: Each labelled end of this tree is a tip. What does a tip represent?

options: A lineage — a species or group of organisms
A common ancestor of several lineages

items.text: A node is a point where branches meet. What does an internal node represent?

options: A common ancestor shared by every lineage below it
The oldest living species on the tree

items.text: What does a branch — a line joining two nodes, or a node and a tip — represent?

options: A lineage persisting through time, ancestor to whatever lies beyond it
A measure of how similar two tips look

items.text: Tap the node where every lineage on this tree last met — its deepest node.
items.note_after: That deepest node is the root: the common ancestor of the whole tree.

items.text: Tap the most recent common ancestor of {set}.
items.note_after: The ancestor sits at the node where their lineages meet. Every tip below that node shares it — not only the named ones.

items.text: This tree draws a time direction. Which way does time run?

options: From the root toward the tips — the tips are the present
From the tips toward the root
The diagram has no time direction

items.text: Order the lettered nodes from oldest to youngest.
items.note_after: A node is older than every node below it. Nodes on separate lineages — like C and P — cannot be ordered: every order consistent with ancestry is accepted.
